To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) biomarkers of inflammation predict mortality in older men, 2) inflammation predicts mortality independently of traditional risk factors, and 3) the predictive ability of inflammation is similar for both cardiovascular and non-cardiovascular causes of death.
inflammation predicts both vascular and nonvascular death in older men.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of inflammation in the development of cardiovascular disease.
understanding the mechanisms of inflammation and the development of novel anti-inflammatory agents.
the identification of biomarkers of inflammation and the development of novel therapeutic approaches to treat inflammation.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
inflammation is a major cause of mortality in men.
the biomarkers of inflammation, in particular hs-CRP, predict both vascular and all-cause mortality, in older men.
the evidence is not yet sufficient to recommend the use of biomarkers in clinical practice.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have shown that the biomarkers of inflammation are predictors of both vascular and non vascular mortality in older men, and that they are independent of other known risk factors.

we have shown that the inflammation biomarkers CRP and IL-6, and the coagulation biomarker fibrinogen, are all independently and significantly associated with mortality in older men, and that the inflammation biomarker IL-6 is also significantly and independently associated with the incidence of cardiovascular disease (CVD).

we have found that the biomarkers of inflammation predict not only cardiovascular disease, but also non-cardiovascular disease mortality in older men, and that this relationship is not mediated by traditional risk factors for cardiovascular disease.
The main takeaway from our work is that
biomarkers of inflammation predict non-vascular and vascular mortality in men aged 65 and older.
inflammation is a strong predictor of death in men, and that this is not limited to cardiovascular death but also includes death from other causes.
inflammation, as measured by the inflammatory biomarkers CRP, IL-6 and TNF-alpha, predicts mortality in older men, and the predictive value is independent of traditional risk factors.
